searchText: <timbeiko> Post-PeerDAS, is there a use case for L2s to have a max blob count *per transaction* exceed, say, 10 blobs/txn? If so, what is it? Is there a higher value that is a reasonable maximum? <vb271828> I lean no <vb271828> and I also support the EIP limiting individual transaction gas consumption (I would put the limit at `2**24` or even `2**23`) <vb271828> there is value in starting to enforce a rule that a tx is a small-sized part of a block and cannot fill up a block <alexanderlhicks> naive question: Is there a reason for enforcing this strictly rather than with some progressive gas cost curve? Why would we want people to distribute their transaction over multiple transactions? That increases block/receipt size. And they can still fill a block, just not with atomicity and ordering guarantees, which is annoying but not a roadblock. <iamchaals> Looks like it would make sense to write it somewhere as a Pattern that standards can refer to... (re @levs57: Hi everyone. I've written some suggestions on improving security committees for rollups (and potential implications for native rollup roadmap). https://hackmd.io/@levs57/HkKKfyEdkl Can any1 tell me if there is a way of turning it into a standard? It is probably too broad for an EIP... maybe RIP? also, if this is standardized it will likely have some major implications for native rollups roadmap, but I want to first see if there is any real interest / feedback on it) <iamchaals> I'm thinking for example of https://entethalliance.github.io/eta-registry/security-levels-spec.html#req-3-timelock-for-privileged-actions <iamchaals> (Which isn't directly specific to L2s, but where it seems it could be relevant) <shemnon> Given the mainnet gas limit I expect we could see limits in excess of 2**25 (32M). So we would need to turn it on as part of a fork definition. This will also be the new limit on contract size if the cap were to be removed (~76k at 2**24 depending on zero count), probably fine for a while. (re @vb271828: and I also support the EIP limiting individual transaction gas consumption (I would put the limit at 2**24 or even 2**23)) <vb271828> yeah I meant including it in a fork (re @shemnon: Given the mainnet gas limit I expect we could see limits in excess of 2**25 (32M). So we would need to turn it on as part of a fork definition. This will also be the new limit on contract size if the cap were to be removed (~76k at 2**24 depending on zero count), probably fine for a while.) <levs57> what should I do / whom should I contact to do this? (re @iamchaals: (Which isn't directly specific to L2s, but where it seems it could be relevant)) <shemnon> I really like the idea, but it is too late for fusaka probably (the testing is the real limiter). But the idea definitely needs to be put out there. (re @vb271828: yeah I meant including it in a fork) <vb271828> yeah I agree, my operating assumption is that fusaka is peerdas + eof best case, peerdas only worst case, only exception is security critical (eg. modexp reprice)
